subject: Web Development
title: App Stores vs. the Open Web
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on App Stores vs. the Open Web.

hook.text: Apple's App Store launched in 2008 with 500 apps. Within a year it had 65,000.

buildup.text: Native apps were faster and smoother than mobile websites. Developers followed the money.

discovery.text: Users spent 90% of mobile time in apps, not browsers. The open web seemed to lose.

twist.text: But apps needed downloads, updates, and store approval. The web had none of that.

climax.text: The tension between closed apps and the open web shaped a decade of technology.

punchline.text: Apps won attention; the web kept its freedom.

quiz.question: How many apps did the App Store launch with in 2008?
